title.narrative: Provision of Essential Integrated Life-Saving Health and Nutrition Services to the vulnerable Populations in Jimaame District

description.narrative: ltpgtThe Somali Lifeline Organization (SOLO) proposes to implement an integrated Health and Nutrition emergency intervention in the flood-affected and underserved communities of Farwaamo, and Towfiq villages in Jamaame District. The project will target approximately 1,550 households, focusing on vulnerable populations including children under five, pregnant and lactating women, displaced families, and households facing severe barriers to accessing essential services due to recurrent flooding, weak health infrastructure, and high acute malnutrition burden.ltbrgtSOLO proposes to restore access to the Essential Package of Health Services (EPHS) through the rehabilitation and operational support of Farwaamo Maternal and Child Health (MCH) facility and the deployment of one mobile outreach teams delivering decentralized primary health care and nutrition services to hard-to-reach settlements. The intervention will deliver 8,563 outpatient department (OPD) consultations across fixed and outreach platforms, providing case management for common illnesses, IMCI services for children under five, maternal and newborn care, sexual and reproductive health services, and emergency referral support.ltbrgtThe project will strengthen prevention of vaccine-preventable diseases through routine immunization services including 100 women receiving Td vaccination and1,677 children (767 girls and 810 boys) receiving age-appropriate EPI vaccines. SOLO will also treat 2,627 cases of acute watery diarrhea, including suspected cholera, supported by strengthened community- and facility-based surveillance and outbreak early warning mechanisms.ltbrgtNutrition interventions will include 12 mass MUAC and bilateral oedema screening campaigns targeting children 6–59 months and pregnant and breastfeeding women, enabling early detection and referral of acute malnutrition cases. SOLO will operationalize one fixed OTP (Towfiq OTP) and one outreach sites (Caawiye 1) to provide outpatient treatment for uncomplicated SAM, linked to stabilization care for complicated cases. The project will facilitate referrals of 4,700 children with MAM (2,500 girls and 2,200 boys) and 900 malnourished pregnant and breastfeeding women to ALIGHT-supported TSFP services, ensuring continuity of care through follow-up and counter-referral mechanisms.ltbrgtTo ensure uninterrupted availability of essential medicines and nutrition supplies, SOLO will coordinate closely with UNICEF for timely provision and replenishment of health and nutrition commodities. Accountability and protection will be reinforced through establishment of three community-based Complaints and Feedback Mechanisms in Farwaamo, and Towfiq, aligned with AAP and PSEA standards, enabling safe reporting of complaints, feedback, and exclusion concerns.ltbrgtThrough this integrated package of lifesaving health, nutrition, surveillance, and accountability interventions, SOLO proposes to reduce preventable morbidity and malnutrition-related mortality while strengthening resilient service delivery for crisis-affected communities in Jamaame District.ltbrgtlt/pgt
